task.text: `Config.get()` is meant to be a double-checked lazy singleton. It is not.
Fix `Config.get()` so that however many threads call it at once, exactly one `Config` is built, and callers never take the class lock once it exists.

items: Keep the `static` field `instance`, the `CREATED` counter and the `onConstruct` hook.
Keep the lazy, double-checked shape: no eager initialization, no holder class, and no `synchronized` on the method.
On the unlocked path read `instance` only once, into a local.
Fix every defect in `get()`, including the one the tests cannot observe directly.

checks.title: Eight racing callers build one Config
A built Config is returned without the lock
The fast path reads the field once

hints.text: Walk through two threads that both see `instance == null`. The first takes the lock and builds. What does the second do when it gets the lock? Then ask what makes a half-built object visible to a reader without a lock.

Check the field again inside the `synchronized` block. Declare the field `volatile` so a reader cannot see a reference before the constructor's writes. On the unlocked path, read the field into a local once and use only that local.

lines: if (local == null) instance = local = new Config();
